subject: Re: Pollen Labs — proposal to exchange promo credits for reserved capacity discount
messages:
From: Aisha Gomez <aisha@pollenlabs.io>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: ethan@pollenlabs.io
Date: Wed, 03 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot credits -> reserved capacity trade?

Hi Marcus —

Quick one: our founders liked Redwood during the pilot and want predictable monthly spend. We have $40k of promo credits remaining in the account that expire in Q3. Would Redwood consider applying those credits toward a 12-month Reserved Capacity commitment (e.g., convert credits to a one-time offset on the first invoice), or do you have a different path to make the economics better for us?

Two constraints:
- Need a clear conversion mechanism that shows month-over-month spend reduction (for our CFO)
- Would prefer an option that preserves some burst capacity during spikes

If this is possible we can speed up procurement next week. Thoughts?

—Aisha
Aisha Gomez
Head of Platform, Pollen Labs
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Gomez <aisha@pollenlabs.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 03 May 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot credits -> reserved capacity trade?

Hi Aisha — thanks for the note and glad Pollen found value. Short answer: yes, we can structure something, but there are a few levers to align on.

Options we typically propose:
1) Credit-as-offset: apply promo credits as a one-time payment against the first month(s) of a Reserved Capacity contract.
2) Milestone release: spread the credit as a monthly offset contingent on usage milestones (gives you more runway but reduces our risk).
3) Hybrid: partial upfront offset + retained burst credits for on-demand spikes.

To make procurement simple for your CFO we normally provide: SOW addendum, an invoice schedule showing the effective discounted ASR (annualized spend rate), and a one-page example of how the credits affect month-one vs month-six.

I'll loop Ben (pricing lead) and Laura (contracts) into this thread and propose a draft that preserves burst for you. Can you confirm the exact remaining promo credit amount and preferred start month?

Best,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of GTM Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: Aisha Gomez <aisha@pollenlabs.io>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: ethan@pollenlabs.io
Date: Thu, 04 May 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot credits -> reserved capacity trade?

Thanks Marcus — we have $38,750 left (system shows $40k but $1,250 was used for a test). Target start is July 1, 2028. Prefer the hybrid approach: something like $25k applied as a one-time upfront offset to the reserved commitment and the remainder preserved as burst credits in a separate bucket usable for on-demand endpoints. If legal requires an amendment it’s OK — procurement prefers a single agreement page that shows the net expected run rate.

Ethan (cc) will be on procurement.

—Aisha
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Gomez <aisha@pollenlabs.io>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 05 May 2028 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot credits -> reserved capacity trade?

Aisha — appreciate the clarity. Attached is a short pricing matrix with three proposal rows (Upfront-offset heavy / Hybrid split / Milestone-based spread). Key points:
- Upfront-offset heavy: apply $25k credit to reduce the first invoice of a 12-month Reserved Capacity contract for a 4-GPU pool. This yields an effective first-month reduction and a committed per-month rate thereafter.
- Hybrid split: $25k upfront + $13,750 retained as a separate 90-day burst bucket for on-demand usage; unused burst expires.
- Milestone-based: spread the $38,750 across 12 months, conditional on meeting 3 monthly usage floors (protects Redwood against churn).

Legal note: the hybrid requires a one-sentence SOW addendum (we'll propose the language) and a DocuSign link for signature. We can also include a unilateral early-conversion clause allowing Pollen to convert remaining burst credits to additional reserved capacity at a pre-agreed rate once you hit sustained utilization.

I'll attach the matrix and a redlineable SOW addendum. If this looks good, Marcus or Laura can push the DocuSign and we can lock the start date as July 1.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-matrix-May2028.xlsx ; SOW-draft-Pollen-2028-05.pdf

Cheers,
Ben
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Ethan Park <ethan@pollenlabs.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Gomez <aisha@pollenlabs.io>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 May 2028 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot credits -> reserved capacity trade?

Ben / Marcus — thanks for the clear options, the hybrid split aligns with our CFO's preference. Two small asks before we sign: 1) can the burst bucket have a 120-day expiry instead of 90 days, and 2) can we add an explicit line in the SOW that unused burst credits can be applied to the final month's invoice if Pollen is under-committed at month 12 (this eases our finance team's approval).

If you can confirm those two edits, we can route the DocuSign today and start July 1.

Ethan Park
Head of Procurement, Pollen Labs
